subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 45-year-old man with alcohol use disorder and a poor diet for 4 months is found to have a macrocytic anemia with hypersegmented neutrophils, a serum folate of 2.1 ng/mL, and a normal serum vitamin B12. His physician explains that, unlike vitamin B12 deficiency, his hematologic abnormality appeared after only a few months of inadequate intake. He has no neurologic deficits, and methylmalonic acid is normal.
question: Which of the following best explains why this deficiency developed so much faster than a vitamin B12 deficiency would under the same dietary conditions?

options.text: Folate is not stored anywhere in the body, so deficiency appears within days of reduced intake
Vitamin B12 is absorbed by passive diffusion and is therefore preserved even when intake is low
Folate requires intrinsic factor for absorption, which alcohol destroys
Vitamin B12 is continuously synthesized and absorbed in the colon
The hepatic folate reserve is small and lasts only months, whereas hepatic vitamin B12 stores last years

explanation_correct: Folate is stored primarily in the liver in a small reserve pool that lasts roughly 3 to 4 months, while vitamin B12 has a very large hepatic reserve that lasts several years. This difference explains why folate deficiency, not B12 deficiency, typically appears after a few months of poor intake or chronic alcohol use. Folate deficiency causes macrocytic anemia with elevated homocysteine and normal methylmalonic acid and typically spares the nervous system.

explanation_incorrect.A: Folate is stored in the liver, although the pool is much smaller than the vitamin B12 pool; deficiency does not develop within days.
explanation_incorrect.B: Vitamin B12 absorption is an active, intrinsic factor-dependent process in the terminal ileum, not passive diffusion.
explanation_incorrect.C: Folate absorption does not require intrinsic factor; intrinsic factor is required for vitamin B12 absorption.
explanation_incorrect.D: Colonic bacteria synthesize vitamin B12 distal to the site of absorption, which is why humans must obtain it from animal products.

educationalObjective: The hepatic folate pool is small and depleted within months, whereas vitamin B12 stores last years, which is why folate deficiency appears earlier during poor dietary intake.
